strings.title: MELT_FORM
strings.subtitle: PLAN 0x30 // CLASS: WIDE
strings.briefing:
Monthly sales sit in three columns: jan, feb, mar. That is easy to read and hard to analyse. Charts, group-bys and joins want one row per product per month.

Melt the table into long form: columns product, month and sales, and none of the old month columns. Every number must survive the move.

In Python, finish with df as the reshaped table. In SQL, build a table named result and that is what gets judged.
strings.task: Turn this wide table (one column per month) into a long one: one row per product per month, with the columns product, month and sales. The jan, feb and mar columns must disappear and no number may be lost.

python: Keep product as the identifier and turn the month columns into rows.
sql: SQLite has no melt. Select each month column on its own and stack the results with UNION ALL.
SELECT product, 'jan' AS month, jan AS sales FROM data  UNION ALL  SELECT product, 'feb', feb FROM data  UNION ALL  ...
CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT product, 'jan' AS month, jan AS sales FROM data UNION ALL SELECT product, 'feb', feb FROM data UNION ALL SELECT product, 'mar', mar FROM data;
